semantically_equivalent_models.justification: Dense neural networks and fully-connected neural networks refer to the same concept where each neuron in one layer is connected to every neuron in the next layer. These terms are often used interchangeably.
Similar to 'fully-connected neural networks', this term is a singular form and semantically equivalent to dense neural networks.
Feed-forward neural networks are considered semantically equivalent as the term 'dense' often implies a single layered or multi-layered feed-forward structure.
Multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) is another term for dense neural networks where multiple layers are fully connected, fitting the definition of dense neural networks.

parent_models.justification: Deep neural networks are a broader category that includes dense neural networks as a subclass where the network consists of multiple layers.
Artificial neural networks is a very broad category that encompasses all types of neural networks including dense neural networks.
Neural network models is a general term that covers any arrangement of neural networks including dense neural networks.
Neural network is a general concept under which dense neural networks fall, as they are a specific type of neural network.

closest_parent_model.justification: Dense or fully-connected layers are commonly used within deep neural networks structures, therefore it serves as the closest parent model.

child_models.justification: A multi-input deep neural network is a type of neural network architecture that can include dense layers for inputs from multiple sources, thus being more specific.

closest_child_model.justification: Incorporating dense layers for handling various input data, multi-input deep neural networks best fits as a specific child model of dense neural networks.

sibling_models.justification: ReLU neural networks are models that specifically use ReLU activation often with dense layers similar to the focus on specific architectures seen in dense neural networks.
These networks are akin to dense neural networks if they employ ReLU as an activation function across dense layers.
Similar to dense networks in structure without specifying non-linear activations or depth, sharing a sibling relationship under a common parent model.
Bayesian neural networks, though differing by including probabilistic connections in layers, share architectural characteristics with dense networks.

closest_sibling_model.justification: The most tightly aligned with dense neural networks in terms of structure, significantly sharing its architectural characteristics without expanding to complex layers such as convolutional or residual connections.

unrelated_models.justification: Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are entirely different in structure utilizing convolutional layers instead of fully-connected layers.
Even though named dense, DenseNet-121 is specific to convolutional operations and connections, distinct from the fully-connected structure of dense neural networks.
Residual networks include skip connections which are a structural innovation not found in dense neural networks.
Deep Q-Networks are specific architectures used in reinforcement learning built on different principles than those for dense neural networks.
Dale's artificial neural networks might refer to a specific implementation or variation distinct from the simply structured dense neural networks.
Fully convolutional networks (FCNs) consist entirely of convolutional layers, differing significantly in structure from dense neural networks.
